exposure: Prepregnancy body mass index (BMI) (< 30 kg/m2 vs. ≥ 30 kg/m2)
cohort: 22,466 women with cerclage placement and live births between 20 and 41 weeks of gestation
finding: Newborns of women with cerclage and prepregnancy BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 had a modestly increased risk of composite neonatal adverse outcomes compared to those with BMI < 30 kg/m2, but no significant difference was found in the risk of composite maternal adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher in women with cerclage and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2.
